paper.title: Automatic Classification of Cancer Pathology Reports: A Systematic Review

evidence.paraphrase: The review identifies and compares NLP systems that classify unstructured cancer pathology reports.
Its benchmarking concerns prediction-task complexity and model families, not validation of a literature search or reachable relevant records.

reviews.rationale: The paper is a domain review of pathology-report classification systems. The abstract does not evaluate literature-search recall, sensitivity against a benchmark set, retrieval ceilings, or candidate-pool reachability, so it does not support the assigned evidence role.

paper.title: A review of machine learning algorithms for identification and classification of non-functional requirements

evidence.paraphrase: The review synthesizes machine-learning approaches for identifying and classifying non-functional requirements.
Precision and recall are described as metrics for classifier performance, not for measuring the recall or sensitivity of a literature search.

reviews.rationale: The apparent recall match refers to supervised classification of requirements documents. Nothing in the abstract evaluates search validation, benchmark-set recovery, relative recall, or reachable literature records.

paper.title: A systematic review and economic evaluation of new-generation computed tomography scanners for imaging in coronary artery disease and congenital heart disease: Somatom Definition Flash, Aquilion ONE, Brilliance iCT and Discovery CT750 HD

evidence.paraphrase: The study reviews diagnostic accuracy and cost-effectiveness of new-generation CT scanners for cardiac imaging.
The reported sensitivity and specificity are diagnostic-test outcomes against invasive coronary angiography, not literature-retrieval outcomes.

reviews.rationale: Although the study reports a systematic database search, its validation target is CT diagnostic accuracy and economic value. Sensitivity here is a clinical-test metric rather than search sensitivity or relative recall, so the assigned evidence role is not supported.

paper.title: Drowsiness Detection in Drivers: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning-Based Models

evidence.paraphrase: The review synthesizes deep-learning models for detecting driver drowsiness in simulated and real driving contexts.
Its evaluation focuses on predictive accuracy, F1-score, dataset transparency, and model-validation protocols rather than literature-search validation.

reviews.rationale: This is a systematic review of predictive models in a road-safety application. The abstract gives no evidence about relative recall, benchmark-based search sensitivity, retrieval ceilings, or reachability of relevant literature.

paper.title: MARKETING CAPSTONE INSIGHTS: LEVERAGING MULTI-CHANNEL STRATEGIES FOR MAXIMUM DIGITAL CONVERSION AND ROI

evidence.paraphrase: The title identifies multi-channel digital marketing conversion and return on investment as the subject.
The synthesis concerns channel coordination, AI personalization, customer-data infrastructure, retargeting, and marketing performance.

reviews.rationale: The paper addresses digital marketing strategy rather than scholarly search, recommendation, or evidence-selection workflows. Its abstract contains no literature-search validation method or reachability outcome relevant to the assigned role.
